title: The Book of Micah Timeline
sub: What Does the LORD Require of You? · Bethlehem Ephrathah
desc: A prophet confronts corrupt leaders, false prophets, and land-seizing elites, while promising a coming ruler born in insignificant Bethlehem and famously summarizing true religion as doing justice, loving faithfulness, and walking humbly with God.

eras.label: Era One · Micah 1
eras.name: The LORD Comes Out of His Dwelling Place — Samaria's Wound Reaches Jerusalem
eras.dates: An oracle against both capitals, Samaria and Jerusalem, opens with the LORD himself marching out to tread the high places of the earth

events.title: The LORD Is Coming Out of His Dwelling Place
events.detail: The LORD descends to tread the mountains themselves because of Jacob's rebellion, centered in Samaria's idolatry, which will be smashed to pieces and reduced to a heap of ruins.

verses.text: “Look, the LORD [Yahweh] is coming out of his dwelling place! He will descend and march on the earth's mountaintops!”

events.title: A Wordplay Lament Across the Towns of Judah
events.detail: Micah mourns barefoot, listing a string of Judean towns whose names are played on in Hebrew to describe their coming fate — the disease that struck Samaria has now reached Jerusalem's own doorstep.

verses.text: “Samaria's disease is incurable. It has infected Judah; it has spread to the leadership of my people and even to Jerusalem!”

eras.label: Era Two · Micah 2
eras.name: Woe to Wicked Schemers — Land Seizers Judged
eras.dates: The powerful who confiscate fields and evict families are confronted directly, followed by a surprising promise of future regathering

events.title: Woe to Wicked Schemers — You Steal a Robe From a Friend
events.detail: The wealthy and powerful who seize fields and evict widows from their homes are told their own schemes will be turned back on them — a disaster from which they cannot free their necks.

verses.text: “They confiscate the fields they desire and seize the houses they want. They defraud people of their homes and deprive people of the land they have inherited.”

events.title: I Will Certainly Gather All of You, O Jacob
events.detail: A sudden turn toward hope: the LORD promises to gather the scattered remnant of Israel like sheep in a fold, with their king himself leading them out.

verses.text: “Their king will advance before them; the LORD [Yahweh] himself will lead them.”

eras.label: Era Three · Micah 3
eras.name: Corrupt Leaders, Prophets, and Priests — Full of the LORD's Spirit
eras.dates: Micah confronts every failed leadership class in Judah before contrasting himself as a prophet genuinely filled with the LORD's Spirit

events.title: You Flay My People's Skin — Corrupt Leaders and False Prophets
events.detail: Judah's leaders are accused, in brutal butchery imagery, of devouring the very people they're supposed to protect, while prophets sell favorable oracles to whoever pays them.

verses.text: “You hate what is good and love what is evil. You flay my people's skin and rip the flesh from their bones.”

events.title: Full of the Courage the LORD's Spirit Gives — Zion Plowed Like a Field
events.detail: Micah contrasts himself, genuinely filled with the LORD's Spirit to confront sin, against leaders who bribe, priests who charge fees, and prophets who read omens for pay while claiming the LORD is still among them.

verses.text: “I am full of the courage that the LORD's [Yahweh's] Spirit gives and have a strong commitment to justice.”
“Because of you, Zion will be plowed up like a field, Jerusalem will become a heap of ruins.”

eras.label: Era Four · Micah 4
eras.name: Nations Streaming to the Mountain of the LORD — Swords Into Plowshares
eras.dates: The prophetic ruin of chapter 3 gives way abruptly to one of Scripture's great visions of future peace among the nations

events.title: They Will Beat Their Swords Into Plowshares
events.detail: In days to come, the LORD's mountain will draw all nations to be taught his ways, ending in a vision of universal disarmament and lasting security for every household under its own vine and fig tree.

verses.text: “Let's go up to the LORD's [Yahweh's] mountain, to the temple of Jacob's God [Elohim]… They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks.”

events.title: You Will Go to Babylon, But There You Will Be Rescued
events.detail: Present agony is compared to labor pains before birth — Zion will go into exile in Babylon, but the LORD promises to deliver her there, giving her the strength to thresh the nations gathered against her.

verses.text: “You will go to Babylon, but there you will be rescued. There the LORD [Yahweh] will deliver you from the power of your enemies.”

eras.label: Era Five · Micah 4:14-5:14
eras.name: Bethlehem Ephrathah — a Ruler Whose Origins Are From Antiquity
eras.dates: The book's most famous prophecy names an insignificant town as the birthplace of a coming, eternal ruler. (The Hebrew text used here counts the verse about the ruler being struck on the cheek as the final verse of chapter 4; most English translations instead open chapter 5 with it, shifting every following verse in this section down by one number in English — a versification difference only, marked inline in the NET text itself.)

events.title: Israel's Ruler Struck on the Cheek
events.detail: A besieged ruler of Israel is struck with a rod on the cheek, a moment of national humiliation immediately followed by the promise of a very different kind of ruler to come. (Numbered 5:1 in most English translations.)

verses.text: “Now slash yourself, daughter surrounded by soldiers! We are besieged! With a scepter they strike Israel's ruler on the side of his face.”

events.title: Bethlehem Ephrathah — a Ruler Whose Origins Are From Antiquity
events.detail: From insignificant Bethlehem will come a ruler over Israel whose origins reach back to ancient days — a prophecy the Gospel of Matthew quotes directly to identify Jesus's birthplace, promising he will shepherd his people by the strength of the LORD. (Numbered 5:2-6 in most English translations.)

verses.text: “Bethlehem Ephrathah, seemingly insignificant among the clans of Judah—from you a king will emerge who will rule over Israel on my behalf, one whose origins are in the distant past.” (Numbered 5:2 in most English translations.)
“He will assume his post and shepherd the people by the LORD's [Yahweh's] strength, by the sovereign authority of the LORD [Yahweh] his God [Elohim].” (Numbered 5:4 in most English translations.)

events.title: A Remnant Among the Nations — Idols and Sorcery Removed
events.detail: The surviving remnant of Jacob is pictured both as refreshing dew and as a devouring lion among the nations, while the LORD promises to purge Israel itself of the horses, fortresses, sorcery, and idols it had wrongly trusted. (Numbered 5:7-15 in most English translations.)

verses.text: “With furious anger I will carry out vengeance on the nations that do not obey me.” (Numbered 5:15 in most English translations.)

eras.label: Era Six · Micah 6
eras.name: The LORD's Covenant Lawsuit — Do Justice, Love Faithfulness, Walk Humbly
eras.dates: A courtroom scene with the mountains as witnesses leads to one of the most quoted single verses in the entire Old Testament

events.title: What Does the LORD Require of You?
events.detail: The LORD brings a covenant lawsuit against Israel, recounting the exodus and his past faithfulness, before answering the question of what sacrifice could possibly satisfy him with a summary of true religion that needs no sacrifice at all.

verses.text: “He has told you, O man, what is good, and what the LORD [Yahweh] really wants from you: to carry out justice, to love faithfulness, and to live obediently before your God [Elohim].”

events.title: Dishonest Scales — the Statutes of Omri and Ahab
events.detail: Specific economic sins are named — rigged scales, deceptive weights, violence in the wealthy quarters — with judgment coming because the nation has followed the corrupt precedents of Omri and Ahab's dynasty.

verses.text: “I do not condone the use of rigged scales or a bag of deceptive weights.”

eras.label: Era Seven · Micah 7
eras.name: Who Is a God Like You? — Compassion That Hurls Sins Into the Sea
eras.dates: The book closes moving from a lament over a society with no faithful people left to one of the most tender statements of God's forgiving character in the prophets

events.title: Faithful Men Have Disappeared — I Will Keep Watching for the LORD
events.detail: Micah laments a society so corrupt that even family bonds have failed, with a man's own household turned into his enemies, yet personally resolves to keep watching for the LORD who alone can deliver him.

verses.text: “I will keep watching for the LORD [Yahweh]; I will wait for the God [Elohim] who delivers me. My God will listen to me.”

events.title: Who Is a God Like You? — Hurling Our Sins Into the Depths of the Sea
events.detail: The book closes in confident hope of restoration and forgiveness, culminating in a rhetorical question celebrating a God unlike any other — one who delights in mercy and will hurl his people's sins into the depths of the sea.

verses.text: “Who is a God [El] like you? Who forgives sin and pardons the rebellion of those who remain among his people?… Who will hurl all our sins into the depths of the sea?”
